headline: Approved a daycare expansion at 1.5 Hood Road; denied a two-family dwelling at 21 Highland Ave; tabled a 156-unit project at 19 Chester Road.
summary: A child daycare will expand into a room at 1.5 Hood Road, and neighbors raised traffic concerns. A clothing alteration business at 2R Richardson Road was also approved, with hours of 8:00 am to 8:00 pm. The 156-unit request at 19 Chester Road was moved to October 1, 2026.
decisions: Accepted two letters about the 1.5 Hood Road daycare, with no opposition.
Granted a variance 5-0 for a child daycare in part of the building at 1.5 Hood Road.
Granted a special exception 5-0 for a clothing alteration and custom design business at 2R Richardson Road, by appointment from 8:00 am to 8:00 pm.
Denied 0-5 a variance for a two-family dwelling on an undersized lot at 21 Highland Ave.
Tabled the variance for a 156-unit, six-building multi-family development at 19 Chester Road until October 1, 2026.

# TOWN OF DERRY

Zoning Board of Adjustment

## MEETING MINUTES – September 17, 2026

**MEMBERS PRESENT**

- Lynn Perkins, Chair
- Craig Corbett, Vice Chair
- Crystal Morin
- Richard Tripp
- James Dietzel

**MEMBERS ABSENT**

**ALTERNATES PRESENT**

- Michael Donlon
- Jason Dragani
- Gaspar Obimba
- Anthony Henry

**ALTERNATES ABSENT**

**CODE ENFORCEMENT**

Keri Owen, Code Enforcement

Minutes prepared by: Eileen Boudreau, ZBA Clerk

## I. CALL TO ORDER:

Mr. Perkins called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the salute to the flag. Instructions were given on safety. He also noted the meeting is audio and video recorded. Mr. Perkins said the ZBA is a quasi-judicial board that reviews appeals for relief from the zoning ordinances and utilizes community development regulations, state statutes, and case law as its guide. Residents that have standing before this board are direct abutters and those who could be aggrieved by the board's decision. The higher courts have ruled that just because you live in town and are a taxpayer does not give you standing to testify on any case that will be before the board this evening.

Mr. Perkins said the board will evaluate any individuals' standing that are not direct abutters before their testimony is given and accepted. He said this is a courtesy announcement for those who may wish to speak and does not want anybody surprised if they are not able to give testimony.

## II. PUBLIC HEARING

26-128

**Applicant:** Etz Hayim Synagogue (Tabled from 9/3/26 meeting)

**Owner:** Andrew Dellapelle

**Parcel ID** 32062-002

1.5 Hood Rd

**Zoned:** MHDR

The applicant is requesting a variance to the terms of Article VI, Section 165-45.A of the Town of Derry Zoning Ordinance to permit the operation of a child group daycare facility within a portion of the existing building.

Mr. Della Pelle introduced himself and read the five criteria.

Mr. Della Pelle said he would like to focus on the uses already present at the same property or nearby. He said the property shares a parking lot with 1 Hood Road, which already hosts an early learning facility with 34 children allowed under state regulations. This is an expansion of that same facility to another room in a different building. It is also a building that previously hosted childcare in the same space. Hartman Learning Center was previously present at 1.5 Hood Road, it was to his understanding, permitted under a different mechanism rather than through the zoning code. Mr. Della Pelle said he has a couple of letters, one from a realtor, Bob Ramalo, and one from Steven Delapelle, his client's brother. The letters say that there is no risk of diminution of value.

Mr. Della Pelle asked if he could give the letters to the board for their review.

Mr. Perkins asked Mr. Della Pelle to give the letters to Code Enforcement. Ms. Owen gave each board member a copy of the letters.

Mr. Corbett made a motion to accept the letters. Mr. Dietzel seconded. All in favor none opposed.

Mr. Perkins asked when the prior learning center left.

Mr. Della Pelle said he believes the lease ended at the end of July, and they got signed the 1st of August.

Mr. Corbett said it is not necessarily a second location, but rather just an expansion of the campus and asked if that is more the way to think of it.

Mr. Della Pelle said these are two buildings that are right next to each other. There are the Etsyheim Synagogue and the Church of the Transfiguration. The Village Early Learning Center at Derry currently has a location inside the Church of the Transfiguration. It is going to be expanding into a room within Etsyheim Synagogue as well.

Mr. Corbett asked if it will be the same name, same school. He asked how much space there was within the synagogue.

Mr. Della Pelle said it is the same license. They have about 3,000 square feet.

Mr. Tripp asked if the people that are going to be working at the daycare are certified by the state and how many people do they expect will be working there.

Mr. Della Pelle Yes. He said they would need two to three staff members on that side with the expansion increasing the capacity for children to 39, there will be 69 total in both locations. They have 34 on the church side, 35 on the synagogue side. They are looking at 16 as soon as they open. They will have two to three staff members on that side and on the church side, about eight. They are all accredited through the state.

Mr. Tripp said he believes Mr. Della Pelle said they have been operating the daycare previously in this facility.

Mr. Della Pelle said they have been open in the Church of the Transfiguration since 2024.

Mr. Perkins asked Mr. Della Pelle if he is staying within state ratios of children to instructors.

Mr. Della Pelle said yes, it is accredited through the state. The fire department and the health inspector gave approval.

Mrs. Morin said she is familiar with the property on the inside and sees it as something that would fit.

Mr. Dragani said he is also familiar with the property. He is not an abutter but is close. He has never seen an issue with the original one.

Ms. Owen discussed the following:

- The applicant is requesting a variance to permit the operation of a child daycare facility within a portion of the existing building.
- The property is located in the Medium-High Density Residential (MHDR) Zoning District, a daycare is not a permitted use, therefore, a variance is required.
- The applicant currently operates The Village Early Learning Center in the lower level of the existing religious facility located on the abutting property at 1 Hood Road. While each property contains its own entrance and parking area, the sites are connected by internal vehicle and pedestrian circulation, allowing access between the two properties.
- Private schools are permitted in MHDR. However, based on the definition of a private school, the age group is K through 12 or older, and the daycare facility falls under that age group category. I would like to make that statement as well.
- The applicant proposes to expand operations by establishing a second daycare location at 1.5 Hood Road within the existing lower level of the building. This area has historically been utilized for educational programming and activities serving parishioner children. No significant modifications to the space are proposed to accommodate the daycare use.
- The property consists of approximately 1.26 acres and contains an existing religious facility. The original site plan was approved by the Planning Board and constructed in 1994.
- If approved by the Board, a site plan amendment will be required to be reviewed and approved by the Planning Board. As part of that process, site circulation and traffic patterns will be evaluated.
- If approved, appropriate permits and inspections will be required.

Ms. Owen said their current use location at 1 Hood Rd was permitted because that was a prior daycare facility previously operating under Headstart. It was looked at as a similar use when the change of use application came through for that property.

## CALL TO PUBLIC

Mr. Perkins made a call to public.

**FAVOR**

No gestures in person.

**OPPOSED**

One gesture in person.

Bruce Brown, 6 Hood Rd said he has 69 years in the town of Derry. He said one of the first questions he would like to ask is how many parking spaces the facility or whatever they plan on doing is going to take up. It is a shared parking lot, but one of the things that has disturbed us since 2007, the original planning board decision had the upper entranceway being one way going in and one way coming out down by the Church of the Transfiguration. By the time the facility was built, somebody made the decision to go one way in, one way out for the synagogue, one way in, one way out for the church. He said it may not seem like a hill of beans, but those entryways are directly opposite driveways of private residences on Hood Road.

Mr. Perkins asked Mr. Brown if his concern was the parking spots or the entrance.

Mr. Brown said all traffic. He likes the fact that when the Derry police come in, they can park in there. He said it helps a lot. He said he has nothing against the idea of the facility, but the neighborhood is turned into a horror show, especially when it comes to traffic. He said there is Nutfield Heights Senior Center right next door that does not have to put up stop signs coming out. There are cars coming out at will and they are right next to the entranceway for the synagogue. The other problem is a stop sign on Lennox Road that nobody understands the word stop. People just go right through the stop sign like there is no problem. They started cross-country up at Hood School and yesterday two kids came along Lennox Road along the sidewalk ready to cross and nobody's stopping for the kids. He has already been up to Hood School to warn them. The other thing in regard to the traffic, if he was living at the Cavanaugh Residence that is right opposite the entranceways for the synagogue in and out, if you were trying to back out that driveway, you would have to have at least nine different checkpoints to watch out for traffic. When you back out you had better look down the street and you had better look directly behind. You had better look right directly over to the stop sign because they are not stopping at the stop sign. Then you go up the street, you have got two driveways for Nutfield Heights Senior Center, which do not have stop signs at all, that they can come out at will. And that also includes the FedEx drivers and the UPS drivers. He cannot back out of his driveway anymore because they have people coming up Perley Road running the stop sign at the top of Perley Road.

Mr. Perkins asked if the synagogue currently operates other than the childcare. He said he can imagine the traffic there if all the spaces get filled.

Mr. Brown said that is correct.

Mr. Perkins asked Mr. Brown if the point he is referring to is that he wants the board to deny this application based on people running stop signs and cross-country activities from the junior high, but that is not necessarily relevant to whether or not the other five criteria apply.

Mr. Brown said there is more to it than that. He said it is the overall traffic pattern, and they call the neighborhood the Pinkerton Thoroughfare. There is school traffic and other neighborhood traffic. This past year, we now have e-bike traffic and kids on electric scooter traffic. It has gotten to be a little bit too much to bear. He said he is afraid that at some point in time, it is going to reach a breaking point, and somebody is going to get hurt or killed.

Mr. Perkins asked if he is anticipating that there will be more traffic from the daycare.

Mr. Brown said he is. I think you have got it right. It sounds like they want to operate during daylight hours Monday through Friday and that is the peak range of a lot of things going on. Pinkerton has adult studies at night. There are church services on the Sunday because the school district is renting out. Now they have redirected the bus traffic in front of the school so that you cannot drive behind the school. It all gets redirected back onto Hood Road and coming down along with everything else.

Mr. Tripp asked Mr. Brown if it is his opinion that denying this variance will resolve these traffic issues.

Mr. Brown said I do not know how much it will be. In my opinion, I am the only one that had the guts to show up at the meeting tonight because everybody else considers it a lost cause. To stand here in front of all these people and say this is a really bad thing, I cannot really predict that. The problem is that where their parking lot is, is right next to what has become one of the more dangerous intersections in our neighborhood. To answer your question, I honestly cannot say.

Mr. Tripp asked Mr. Brown if he believes that the installation of traffic control signs would resolve some of his problems.

Mr. Brown said I think it would. I really do not know. The thing that really scares me the most is where they have got the sidewalk. It comes from the sidewalk on the Lennox Street side, and it stops right next to the driveway of Nutfield Heights. I really do not know. Maybe.

Mr. Tripp said it sounds like a couple of stop signs would help resolve the problems Mr. Brown has with the traffic.

Mr. Brown said I think the only stop signs that you can put up are already up. What still bothers me about Nutfield Heights is why do not they even have a yield sign up, never mind a stop sign.

Mr. Perkins asked Mr. Brown if he is referring to Nutfield Heights and their exiting out of their parking lot onto the street. He said he believes that it is a private parcel.

Mr. Brown said that is what he is wondering.

Mr. Perkins asked Mr. Brown if overall his concern is traffic flow in and out and the abundance of parking spaces.

Mr. Brown said traffic flows in and out and everybody in the summertime just does whatever they want to do whenever they want to do it. I just pray to God nobody gets hurt.

Mr. Perkins said they respect the concern and appreciate him for bringing it forward.

Mr. Della Pelle said they will be adding two to three staff if they are fully enrolled. They are looking at an additional two to three parking spaces throughout the day. There would be changes at the times of drop-off, between about 6:30 in the morning to 9:00 in the morning for the drop-off, and pickups are between 4:30 and 5:30 at night. There is some overlap with the nearby schools, Grinnell and Hood, but not total overlap, particularly in the evenings. In addition, I believe Ms. Owen had made mention that this may require a site plan amendment and changes to circulation within the parking lot, which would at that time, the planning board would be able to assess whether there is a need for additional traffic controls coming out.

Mr. Perkins asked about the ratios Mr. Tripp had asked about and if it is going to be 16 more children.

Mr. Della Pelle said the expansion can hold up to 35 via state regulations. He said they would not be bringing it up to 35. The max would probably be a 1 to 8 ratio, so 24 kids would probably be the max.

Mr. Perkins asked if they were looking at 24 additional cars per day other than staff twice during the day.

Mr. Della Pelle said unlike the schools it is not when school gets out of session, everyone leaves at one time. When parents need to drop off prior to work, they might get three, four, five, maybe six tops. And then same thing on the back end, you might have like 6 to like 10 cars max at a given time.

Mr. Perkins said you might have three cars, four cars leaving at all in the same within three minutes of each other, but then you might not have anything for another 10 minutes.

Mr. Tripp asked what the operating hours and days are.

Mr. Della Pelle said it is Monday through Friday from 7:00am to 5:30pm.

Mr. Dragani asked if Mr. Della Pelle said drop-off is between 6:30 and 9:00 in the morning.

Mr. Della Pelle said drop-off is around 7:00am but cannot give a direct time because parents work different hours. He said about 7:00 to 9:00 is the drop-off and pickup is around 4:00 to 5:30.

## MOTION TO ENTER DELIBRATION

Mr. Tripp made a motion to enter deliberation.

Seconded by Ms. Morin All in favor, none opposed.

Mr. Perkins said Mr. Brown, the abutter brings forward concerns about traffic violations relative to this site and traffic flow in and out of the site. In his view the amount or the abundance of traffic is not such as he might see coming in and out of Pinkerton Academy at 2:30 in the afternoon. He is appreciative of his points of view for safety. If there are any blind spots, he thinks that the planning board amendments could help mitigate that. Unlike the zoning board, the planning board does walkthroughs and site walks. Any concerns that Mr. Brown was good enough to bring forward to this board may get addressed at that point, and his voice could be heard at that point as well.

Mr. Corbett said he has been up and down this road daily over the last three weeks. My son's been doing the athletics within Hood, familiar with what Mr. Brown's been detailing as well. And I think to that point, I have not noticed the existing daycare there. As I come down the road, the big traffic, or the big amount of traffic I see is the six teams who get let out at the same time up at the middle school. I do not see that an additional 24 kids in the daycare are going to add anything negative. Overall, for the use of an expanded use, I think this is the perfect location for it to utilize an empty space during the week. To the point of drop-off, you see about two or three cars at your drop-off time. I do not think any of the five criteria are really an issue here.

Mr. Dietzel said I share Mr. Brown's concerns. I drive through that neighborhood a lot, and a lot of the traffic rules are not either obeyed or well enforced. I am trying to look at it strictly from a zoning standpoint and weighing this against the five criteria. I think that most of Mr. Brown's concerns are longstanding and are there whether or not the daycare center comes into existence or not. I think based on

## MOTION

the size and the scope of what is being proposed by the applicant, I do not think that the problem which exists already will be significantly increased based on what they want to do. I agree with Mr. Corbett, I see that all five criteria are met.

Mr. Tripp said the problems that Mr. Brown brought up; I do not think that the daycare is the source of those problems. I think the problems that Mr. Brown brought up are long existing and that expanding the size of the daycare would increase those traffic issues. I think that Mr. Brown should go back to the Traffic Safety Committee and see if they can do something about this. I do not see where approving this variance will increase the problem.

Ms. Morni said I agree with what Mr. Corbett stated.

## MOTION TO LEAVE DELIBRATION

Mr. Corbett made a motion to leave deliberation.

Seconded by Mr. Tripp All in favor, none opposed.

## MOTION

Ms. Morin made a motion on case 26-129 to grant a variance to the terms of Article VI, Section 165-45.A of the Town of Derry Zoning Ordinance to permit the operation of a child group daycare facility within a portion of the existing building.

Parcel ID: 32062-002 Zoned: MHDR

as presented with the following conditions:

1. Subject to obtaining all state and town permits and inspections.

Mr. Corbett reviewed the finding of fact as follows:

Heard September 16th, 2026. The ZBA heard the application of Andrew Delapelle concerning the property located at 1.5 Hood Road, parcel ID 32062-002. Notice was provided to the immediate abutters per statute, and the board received testimony from the applicant and legal counsel, town staff, and abutters. ## 26-129

**Applicant:** Zoe A. Meyer

**Owner:** Heidi E. Meyer

Parcel ID 10062-003R

2B Richardson Rd

Zoned: LDR

The applicant is requesting a Special Exception to the terms of Article VI, Section 165-48.A.1 of the Town of Derry Zoning Ordinance to allow the operation of a clothing alteration and custom design business at the residence.

Heidi Meyer introduced herself as Zoe’s Business Manager and introduced her daughter Zoe Meyer. Heidi read the questions and provided answers.

Mr. Dragani asked what the hours of operation at this location will be and what hours are going to be accepted appointments.

Ms. Meyer said it would be by appointment only and would expect not to go past 7 o'clock at night. It could be seven days a week.

Mr. Perkins asked how many days for the record.

Ms. Meyers said Zoe would be available seven days a week. She might have a late afternoon, early evening appointment with someone. On Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, she would be available all day.

Mr. Perkins asked if it was possible for the hours to be 8:00 am to 7:00 pm.

Ms. Meyers said they would be fine with that stipulation.

Mr. Corbett asked if 8:00 am to 8:00 pm would be better. Thinking about prom season.

Ms. Meyers agreed 8:00 am to 8:00 pm.

Mr. Dragani has a follow-up. He asked if this was just for the alterations and not online.

Ms. Meyers said she is building a brand where she sells Western clothing and accessories online. She does participate in fashion shows and occasionally needs to have models come to the house to be fitted. So that would be additional.

Mr. Tripp said I understand you have a Condex and asked if it was a shared driveway.

Ms. Meyers said yes. It is not a shared driveway.

Ms. Owen discussed the following:

- The applicant is requesting a Special Exception to allow the operation of a clothing alteration and custom design business at the residence.
- The property is located in the Low Density Residential Zoning District (LDR). The types of home businesses permitted by special exception in LDR specifically include “Artist, artisan or craftsman.”
- The property contains an existing two-family residence on a 0.94 acre lot. The residence contains approximately 1,404 sq ft of living area, and the clothing business will operate within an existing 192 sq ft detached shed located on the property.
- If signage is proposed, a sign permit will be required.

## CALL TO PUBLIC

Mr. Perkins made a call to public.

## FAVOR

No gestures in person.

## OPPOSED

No gestures in person.

## MOTION TO ENTER DELIBRATION

Mr. Corbett made a motion to enter deliberation.

Seconded by Mr. Tripp All in favor, none opposed.

Mr. Corbett said this is a special exception versus the variance, and we have to look at it differently. This is more of checking the boxes as I go through them. The only potential concern that I had was as we got into it, normally, when we have had a couple mother-daughter combos, but they have been owning the business together, whereas this one was separate. But being that Zoe does have this claimed as her legal residence, it checks all nine boxes. It is very clearly allowed by definition. I think the 8 to 8 that they offered up is more than fair. I see absolutely no issues with this.

## MOTION TO LEAVE DELIBRATION

Mr. Corbett made a motion to leave deliberation.

Seconded by Mr. Tripp All in favor, none opposed.

## MOTION

Parcel ID: 10062-003R Zoned: LDR

as presented with the following conditions:

1. Subject to obtaining all state and town permits and inspections.
2. By appointment only, 7 days a week between 8:00 am-8:00 pm

Seconded by: Mr. Tripp All in favor, none opposed.

Finding of Fact:

Heard September 16th, 2026. The ZBA heard the application for a special exception from Zoe Meyer at the property located at 2R Richardson Road, Parcel ID 10062-003R. The applicant is requesting a special exception to allow the operation of a clothing alteration and custom design business at the residence. Voting Members:

Ms. Morin Yes
Mr. Corbett Yes
Mr. Dietzel Yes
Mr. Tripp Yes
Mr. Perkins Yes

## 26-130

**Applicant:** Robert Burge

**Owner:** NH Lexx LLC

Parcel ID 26240

21 Highland Ave

Zoned: MHDR

The applicant is requesting a variance to the terms of Article VI, Section 165.45.B.1.a.ii of the Town of Derry Zoning Ordinance to permit a two-family dwelling on a lot with less than the minimum required lot area per dwelling unit.

Robert Bursch, owner of New Hampshire Lex, LLC introduced himself and read the five criteria.

Mr. Bursch said he is the current owner of 21 Highland. It was a property that was purchased in major disrepair. We are looking to continue the renovation of the existing structure with the current footprint of where it is. We are looking to add where there was an existing building that was falling down that was attached to the property, which is noted as the existing foundation on the rear. We have brought that down to the foundation. It was completely uninhabitable. And we are proposing in that area to build a 30 by 30 additional unit, which will be attached to the existing structure that we are renovating. Height would be the same. We do not have all the architectural stuff done for it, but the height and everything would be the same as the existing structure next door.

Mr. Perkins asked if it was a 30 by 30 footprint and if it was going to be two stories.

Mr. Bursch said it is a 30 by 30 footprint. He said that is what they propose. Currently, the property has a sloping lot, which we will maintain. We will put a full foundation in. The existing foundation that is noted on the plot plan most likely will have to be 100% removed. We will pour in the exact same. It is cinder block that has been crumbled.

Mr. Perkins said I am noticing that the existing structure is on a cinder block foundation as well.

Mr. Bursch said that is correct. That foundation, there has no issues. It is the one in the back that was attached to it.

Mr. Perkins asked when Mr. Bursch closed on the property and when they razed the building.

Mr. Bursch said he closed on the property approximately a year ago and they razed the building immediately. The walls were falling in, and they pulled permits to start working on the structure and noted that we were going to be taking that down. It was to the point that the floor was completely caved in.

Mr. Perkins said understanding they may have some abutter input that may not be consistent with your testimony.

Ms. Owen said she will provide the staff I report but unfortunately our historic records of this file are lacking. She will explain what we have.

Ms. Owen discussed the following:

- The applicant is requesting a variance to permit a two-family dwelling on a lot with less than the minimum required lot area per dwelling unit.
- The property is located in the Medium High Density Residential Zoning District (MHDR) which allows for the construction of a two-family dwelling with a required lot area of 10,000 square feet per dwelling unit, or 20,000 square feet for a two-family dwelling.
- The property in question contains approximately 11,325 sq ft where 20,000 sq ft is required
- The property is serviced by municipal water and sewer.
- If approved, appropriate permits and inspections will be required.

As mentioned, there is one letter in the file in opposition that was received.

Mr. Perkins asked if the property was it listed as a two-family Mr. Bursch purchased it or was it a private sale between him and the seller.

Mr. Bursch said it was a private sale. It was a real estate agent who is a family member.

Mr. Perkins asked Ms. Owen if it was listed as a two-family and if there is any idea how old the extra building was. He asked if there is any validity to the fact that there was a kitchen and electrical in the building.

Ms. Owen said it is listed in the assessing record as a single family. She said she is unfamiliar with the original layout of the building. I am unable to locate or reference demo permits or permits that are being mentioned this evening. I do not have anything on record for recent work. I can tell you approximately it was built around 1900, the original structure. The addition, I am not sure if that was original or constructed at a later date. Unfortunately, we do not have the record in our file.

Mr. Perkins asked if Ms. Owen is she said there is a demolition permits for this.

Ms. Owen said that is correct.

Mr. Bursch said they have a building permit for the structure that it had already fallen in. To the point that the roof was compromised. There was a tree right through it. We removed the broken wood and the broken windows. You could not walk on the floor. You could see right down, there was a washing machine in one area that had fallen all the way to the basement. Roof was caved in on it. We left the foundation. The foundation is intact.

Mr. Perkins said he did see where the foundation was on his drive by.

Mr. Dietzel asked why they are not building a single-family house on the parcel.

Mr. Bursch said they do rentals. We looked at the property and purchased it privately. It was never marketed as a two-family. We looked at it and it had separate electric and it had more than enough parking spaces on the front of the property. We came in and we were trying to obtain a second unit. There are plenty of properties in that neighborhood with larger lots that have existing two-families, and there's also properties in that neighborhood with smaller lots that have two-families.
